front_matter.title_page: Tangkhul Constitution & Civic Rights Primer: Indiawui Samvidhan kala Hao Rights (2005)
front_matter.preface: Empowering indigenous communities requires accessible legal literacy in their mother tongue. This primer renders fundamental constitutional concepts—sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity—into dignified Tangkhul legal prose, harmonizing constitutional democracy with customary village court (*Hangva*) jurisprudence.

chapters.title: The Preamble to the Constitution of India (Samvidhan Preamble)
chapters.summary: Solemn translation of the Preamble into classical Tangkhul civic diction.
chapters.english_translation: WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.
grammar_notes: Constitutional legal compounding: 'Uningnao ngayeikasa' for Fraternity.
Solemn declarative formula: 'adopt salaga, enact salaga... miserie'.
exercises: Memorize the Tangkhul translation of the Preamble.
Identify the four cardinal constitutional pillars in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Fundamental Rights (Article 14 to 32)
chapters.summary: Rights to equality, freedom of speech, personal liberty, and constitutional remedies translated for Tangkhul citizens.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Fundamental Rights (Hao Citizen Rights):
1. Article 14: Law-wui ngalemli mikumo pupup khangayam leisaye (Equality before law).
2. Article 19: Tui hangkhavai, phanit sakhavai, kala union kasakhavai mathat (Freedom of speech & assembly).
3. Article 21: Ringkapha kala personal liberty huikhuikhavai rights.
4. Article 25: Chotkhangashit kala reot-kasavai freedom.
5. Article 29-30: Minority language, script kala culture ngashankhavai rights.
6. Article 32: Supreme Court kala High Court-li writ petition eina rights huikhuikhavai remedies.
chapters.english_translation: Overview of Part III of the Constitution: Equality before the law, six freedoms of Article 19, protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21, freedom of religion under Article 25, minority cultural and linguistic protections under Articles 29-30, and the right to constitutional remedies under Article 32.
grammar_notes: Legal rights nomenclature: 'rights ngashankhavai' (safeguarding of rights).
Universal quantifier: 'mikumo pupup' (all citizens without exception).
exercises: Why are Articles 29 and 30 crucial for Tangkhul linguistic preservation?

chapters.title: Customary Law, Village Courts (Hangva) & Article 371
chapters.summary: Integration of indigenous tribal customary law, village councils, and constitutional special autonomy provisions.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Hao Ngashan kala Constitutional Protection:
Tangkhul village pupupli traditional council hoda Hangva (Village Court) leisaye. Awungshina headman hoda court-wui tui khak-kasaye. Article 371A kala 371C-wui provisions eina tribal customary laws, land ownership (ngalei khangayei), and civil justice-li constitutional autonomy miserie. Hangvawui decisions customary law eina sashung-khalang, formal law courtsna chichi respect salaga ngashane.
chapters.english_translation: Tribal customary governance operates through the Hangva (Village Council and Court) presided over by the Awungshi (village chief/headman). Constitutional provisions including Article 371 safeguard indigenous customary laws, land tenure systems, and traditional conflict resolution from arbitrary legislative interference.

8. Ngalei khangayei -- Land tenure rights (भूमि अधिकार)

thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and
of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the
dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; IN
OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do
HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.
